$comment: Activity-detection patterns, read from here rather than compiled in.
An agent's wording is not ours to control: Claude, Codex and the rest
reword their prompts whenever they like, and a changed phrase used to mean
the app no longer noticed that agent waiting for an answer — fixable only
by a new release. This file ships inside the binary as a fallback, and the
app refreshes it from the repository in the background, so a wording change
can be fixed by editing this file alone.
waiting: lowercase substrings matched against the pane's last lines. Keep
them distinctive: a phrase that also appears in ordinary output makes the
spinners: characters an agent animates while it works. Presence of one is
the primary busy signal, so a character the agent prints for other reasons
would make it look permanently busy.
version: increment when changing anything here. The app only replaces its
copy with a higher version, so an older file cannot overwrite a newer one.

codex.$comment: Codex phrases its approval prompt its own way; the generic wording never appears, so those alone left every Codex question undetected.
waiting: tell codex what to do differently
